name: WA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Long-serving incumbent Adam Smith with a large fundraising edge
Challenger Doug Basler's minimal campaign resources
model.rationale: The D+22 district, Smith's incumbency and roughly 19-to-1 fundraising advantage over Basler, and markets pricing Smith at about 96% all point to an easy incumbent win, so the fundamentals-based margin stands.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Basler or unusually low turnout could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Adam Smith, a Democrat who has held this Seattle-area House seat for many years, faces Republican Doug Basler in the general election. The district leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 22 points, and Smith advanced to the general as the incumbent with strong name recognition and a well-funded campaign. He has raised nearly $1.9 million and holds more than $860,000 in cash, while Basler has raised under $100,000 with almost nothing left on hand and no outside support on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Smith's chances around 96%. The combination of the district's lean, incumbency, and the lopsided money gap makes this a Safe Democratic seat, with the main uncertainty limited to the size of the winning margin rather than the winner.
